title: API Gateway with Spring Cloud Gateway
description: Route requests, enforce security, and add cross‑cutting concerns with a gateway.

slides.title: The Gateway Pattern 🚪
slides.content:
# Single Entry Point

An **API Gateway** sits between clients and microservices. It:
- Routes requests to the appropriate service.
- Enforces security (authentication/authorization).
- Aggregates responses.
- Handles cross‑cutting concerns (logging, rate limiting, CORS).

Spring Cloud Gateway is a reactive, non‑blocking gateway built on Project Reactor.

quizData.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical responsibility of an API Gateway?
quizData.explanation: API Gateway handles traffic management, but business data is stored in microservices, not the gateway.

slides.title: Setting Up Spring Cloud Gateway
slides.content:
Create a new Spring Boot project with `spring-cloud-starter-gateway`. Then define routes in `application.yml`:

```yaml
spring:
  cloud:
    gateway:
      routes:
        - id: user-service
          uri: lb://user-service   # lb:// uses service discovery
          predicates:
            - Path=/users/**
        - id: order-service
          uri: lb://order-service
          predicates:
            - Path=/orders/**
```

Now any request to `/users/**` is forwarded to the user‑service, and `/orders/**` to order‑service.

slides.title: Adding a Custom Filter
slides.content:
You can add filters to modify requests/responses. Example: add a request header.

```yaml
spring:
  cloud:
    gateway:
      routes:
        - id: user-service
          uri: lb://user-service
          predicates:
            - Path=/users/**
          filters:
            - AddRequestHeader=X-Request-Source, gateway
```

Or write a custom filter class implementing `GlobalFilter` to log requests.

slides.title: Reactive Under the Hood
slides.content: Spring Cloud Gateway is built on **Spring WebFlux** (non‑blocking). It's lightweight and can handle many concurrent connections. Make sure your dependencies are compatible (no Tomcat, use Netty).
